deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Vertheilung einer elastischen Flüssigkeit die sich blos durch ihre eigne Attraction zusammenhält' (distribution of an elastic fluid, i.e. a gas, held together only by its own gravitation). In modern terms this is the equilibrium of a self-gravitating isothermal gas sphere. p is the density, which for an isothermal gas is proportional to pressure (Boyle's law). m(r) is the enclosed mass. Units are chosen so that the central density and all physical constants equal 1.

(A) First attempt.
- Equations: -dp = m p dr and dm = p r^2 dr. Gravity here is taken as m instead of m/r^2.
- Substitute q = 1/p. Then dq = -dp/p^2 = m q dr, so m = q'/q.
- From dm = r^2 dr/q we get q dm = r^2 dr.
- Differentiating m = q'/q: q m' = q'' - q'^2/q, hence q'' = q'^2/q + r^2.
- [mine] Putting q = t^2 gives q' = 2tt' and q'' = 2t'^2 + 2tt''. Then 2t'^2 + 2tt'' = 4t'^2 + r^2, i.e. t t'' = t'^2 + r^2/2 (Gauss writes the derivative as ∂t/∂r).
- Series with q(0) = 1, q'(0) = 0: q = 1 + r^4/12 + r^8/504 + r^12/99792 + r^16/167650560.
  - In factorial form: 1 + 2r^4/4! + 80r^8/8! + 4800r^12/12! + 124800r^16/16!.
  - As a continued product: 1 + r^4/12 + r^8/(12·42) + r^12/(12·42·198) + r^16/(12·42·198·1680).
- t = sqrt(q) = 1 + r^4/24 + r^8/8064 - r^12/6386688 + ...
  - 8064 = 24·336 and 6386688 = 24·336·792.
  - In factorial form: 1 + r^4/4! + 5r^8/8! - 75r^12/12! + 38025r^16/16!.

(B) 'Oder richtiger' (or, more correctly), with Newtonian gravity m/r^2.
- Equations: -dp = m p dr/r^2 and dm = p r^2 dr.
- [mine] With p = e^{-psi} this becomes (1/r^2)(r^2 psi')' = e^{-psi}, the isothermal Emden equation.
- Gauss's series:
  - p = 1 - r^2/6 + r^4/45 - 61r^6/22680 + 629r^8/2041200.
  - 1/p = 1 + r^2/6 + r^4/180 - r^6/11340 - 11r^8/2041200. The r^8 term is wrong; see errors.
  - m = ∫p r^2 dr = r^3/3 - r^5/30 + r^7/315 - 61r^9/204120 + 629r^11/22453200.
- Next he writes m^2 in the form (1/30)(2·5/3)r^6 - (1/315)(4·7/4)r^8 + (61/204120)(6·9/5)r^10 - (629/22453200)(8·11/6)r^12.
  - [mine] This follows from the identity m m' = 2r m' - r^2 m''. It holds because m' = r^2 p and m'' = 2rp - mp.
  - So if m = Σ c_k r^{2k+3}, then m^2 = -Σ c_k (2k)(2k+3)/(k+2) r^{2k+4}.
  - It reproduces m^2 = r^6/9 - r^8/45 + ..., so it is a neat check or shortcut.
- He then writes r^3/(3m) = 1 + r^2/10 + r^4/2100 - r^6/(…). This is the reciprocal of the mean density in units of the central density.

(C) 'Einfacher geschrieben' (written more simply), with powers of r^2/3 separated out.
- p = 1 - (1/2)(r^2/3) + (1/5)(r^4/9) - (61/840)(r^6/27) + (629/25200)(r^8/81) - (2869/346500)(r^10/243).
- 1/p = 1 + (1/2)(r^2/3) - (1/20)(r^4/9) - (1/420)(r^6/27) + (1/6300)(r^8/81) ∓ (19/1386000)(r^10/243).
  - The last sign is under an ink blot; 4620 is struck out and replaced by 1386000.
- [mine] Read literally, this second line is not consistent with the earlier 1/p series. The leading terms of the earlier 1/p are +r^2/6 and +r^4/180. Here the factors give +r^2/6 and -r^4/180, and the r^6 and r^8 coefficients also differ from the earlier ones in magnitude.
  - The only clean correspondence is p = Σ (r^2/3)^k times the listed factors, which the p line does satisfy.
  - So the 1/p line probably uses some other convention or carries signs/numbers I cannot reconstruct. I flag it rather than treat it as confirming or correcting the earlier series.
errors: Part (A) uses gravity m instead of m/r^2 (dimensionally wrong for Newtonian attraction). Gauss himself replaces it with the correct form under 'Oder richtiger'. The algebra and series in (A) are nevertheless correct for the equations as written (checked through r^16 for both q and t).
In the first 1/p series of part (B), the r^8 term -11/2041200 is wrong. By my working the coefficient of e^{psi} at r^8 is +4/2041200 = +1/510300, with denominator equal to 6300·81.

The 'Einfacher geschrieben' 1/p line, read literally (factor times (r^2/3)^k), does not reproduce the earlier 1/p series. The r^4 sign is opposite (-1/180 vs +1/180), and the r^6 and r^8 magnitudes differ (1/11340 vs 1/420·27, 4/2041200 vs 1/6300·81). The intended convention is unclear, so this line should not be counted as verified.
In r^3/(3m) the r^6 term should be -1/121500. Exact working: 61/68040 - 2/1050 + 1/1000 = -14/1701000. The manuscript appears to read 1/1215000, an extra 0 (or a misreading).
The 1/p r^10 coefficient is partly obscured by an ink blot. A struck denominator 4620 is replaced by 1386000. The sign and value of this term are unconfirmed (see the 1/p line issue above).

results.what: Formulation of the hydrostatic equilibrium of a self-gravitating isothermal gas sphere: -dp = m p dr/r^2, dm = p r^2 dr, equivalent to the isothermal Emden equation (1/r^2)(r^2 psi')' = e^{-psi}.
results.modern_name: Isothermal Lane–Emden (Emden–Chandrasekhar) equation / isothermal gas sphere
results.usually_credited_to: A. Ritter (1878–83) and R. Emden ('Gaskugeln', 1907); polytropes J. H. Lane (1870); Kelvin (1887); later Chandrasekhar (1939)

results.what: Power-series solution regular at the centre: density 1 - r^2/6 + r^4/45 - 61r^6/22680 + 629r^8/2041200 - 2869r^10/84199500, with mass function m(r).
results.modern_name: Series expansion of the isothermal Emden function near the centre

results.what: Identity m m' = 2r m' - r^2 m'' used to obtain m^2 term by term; and the mean-density ratio r^3/(3m).
results.modern_name: First integral / homology-type relation for the Emden equation; mean-to-central density ratio

results.what: Substitutions q = 1/p and q = t^2 with series for the provisional, incorrect force law.
results.modern_name: Series solution of a nonlinear ODE

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss explicitly sets up the equilibrium of a gas sphere held together by its own gravitation under Boyle's law, which is the isothermal Emden equation. He then computes its central series correctly to r^10. This is usually associated with Lane (1870), Ritter and Emden (1878–1907). If the folio dates near 1809, it anticipates that line of work by decades. It is only a series computation, with none of the deeper theory (singular solution, infinite mass, homology invariants), and I don't know whether Gauss scholars have already noted it, so I keep the score moderate.

checkable.asserts: q solves q''=q'^2/q+r^2 through r^14 (should be O(r^16))
isothermal Emden series for density p satisfies p'=-m p/r^2 through r^9
1/p = 1 + r^2/6 + r^4/180 - r^6/11340 + r^8/510300 + ... (r^8 coefficient +4/2041200, not -11/2041200); compare also with the 'Einfacher geschrieben' 1/p line, which as written does not match
Gauss's m^2 expression matches m^2 through r^12

transcription_corrections: 'Oder richtiger' is correct and means 'or, more correctly'; it introduces the corrected force law m/r^2.
In r^3/(3m) the last denominator should mathematically be 121500; the manuscript seems to read 1215000.

In the final 1/p line, the denominator 4620 is struck through and replaced by 1386000; the sign before 19 is hidden by the ink blot. The 1/p 'Einfacher geschrieben' line as a whole does not match the earlier 1/p series under a literal reading, so its transcription (signs and factors) should be re-checked against the image.
The 'mm' line is m^2 written as products c_k·(2k)(2k+3)/(k+2); the transcription is accurate.
